title: Spring Break Camper's Spiritual Growth
summary: A Spring Break camper shares how God taught them individually and within their group, and found the culture and environment uplifting and spirit-filled.
snippet: 'God taught me a lot individually and within my group. The culture and environment is also very uplifting and spirit-filled.' - Spring Break Camper

title: Crisis Fund Established During Pandemic
summary: Catholic Charities NH set up the Crisis Fund to provide direct assistance to vulnerable residents during the COVID-19 pandemic, raising $380,332 as of September 2020.
snippet: That's why Catholic Charities NH swiftly set up the Catholic Charities NH Crisis Fund to provide direct assistance to the state's most vulnerable residents

title: Ripple Support Group for Loved Ones
summary: A six-week series of free education and support for loved ones of those experiencing substance abuse. The group provides a safe space to learn about addiction, recovery, and treatment, and members support each other in their roles as family and friends.
snippet: A six-week series of weekly education and support for loved ones (18 years old and above) experiencing substance abuse and are seeking an understanding of addictions and support.

title: Tricia Hall's Drive for GDCDB
summary: Tricia Hall from Abundant Life Ministry organized a drive for the Greater DC Diaper Bank in August, contributing to the organization's supply.
snippet: Tricia Hall from Abundant Life Ministry did a drive for the GDCDB in August.

title: First-Time Food Delivery Recipient's Gratitude
summary: A first-time food delivery recipient called the team in tears to express her gratitude, saying the delivery had everything she needed.
snippet: A first-time food delivery recipient called to let our team know what it meant to her. In tears she said, 'Thank you. This delivery had everything I needed.'

title: Vanesa's Path to Stability After Homelessness
summary: Vanesa was introduced to FloCrit after having her son Gabriel. After a fire left her family homeless, FloCrit's Housing Department arranged a hotel stay and later helped her secure a Section 8 apartment. She graduated in 2024 and now lives with her boyfriend and two sons in safe housing.
snippet: Vanesa was introduced to Florence Crittenton Services at the hospital after having her son, Gabriel. 'I was scared. I didn't know what to do,' she recalled.

title: Phillip Garcia's Long-Term Service as Policy Council Chairperson
summary: Phillip Garcia served as Chairperson for the MSHS Policy Council for two consecutive program years, balancing his role with a busy schedule as a track driver. His son attended the Migrant classroom at the Preston Green Learning Center.
program: Migrant & Seasonal Head Start Policy Council
snippet: Phillip served as the Chairperson for the MSHS Policy Council for the 20/21 & 21/22 program years. ... He was very dedicated to serving the program and took time out of his busy schedule of track driving to attend the meetings.

title: Tim's Forever Home at Palo Duro
summary: Tim, diagnosed with multiple mental illnesses including PTSD, found NSO's Palo Duro program in 2007. He considers it his forever home and a family where residents encourage each other.
snippet: Palo Duro is a family and we all lean on each other. It's a community and we all encourage each other. I plan on staying here forever.

title: Client Finds Warmth and Support
summary: A client expresses gratitude for the welcoming environment at The Pantry, noting that the staff and volunteers made them feel at ease. They appreciate the in-person shopping experience and the dignity it provides.
snippet: It can be very difficult to disclose to others when your family is struggling. Everyone at The Pantry has been so warm and welcoming that my anxiety about the process is gone. I absolutely love the in-person shopping experience.

title: Elderly Customer Praises Homemaker
summary: An elderly customer expressed high satisfaction with their HRA Homemaker, describing them as 'one in a million' and stating 'Love Her.' The homemaker service helps seniors maintain independence at home.
snippet: What customers say about their HRA Homemaker -" One in a million" " Love Her"

title: Holiday Helper and Thanksgiving Package Participant
summary: A participant expresses deep gratitude for the Holiday Helper and Thanksgiving Package programs, noting how the support made their children happy on Christmas morning and how kind and caring the MFCC staff are.
snippet: I just want to reach out and say how much I appreciate you all for setting up Christmas [Holiday Helper] and Thanksgiving help for those in need. Myself and my oldest daughter got help for the holidays through you guys. I really just wanted to thank you all so much! [I just want to say] how grateful we are and how happy our kids will be on Christmas morning. MFCC you guys are truly amazing, I've never dealt with such kind and caring people until I came across MFCC. You truly are saviors for many of us and we greatly appreciate each and every one of you. Thanks again and happy holidays

title: D'Metrique Godbolt: From Power Scholar to Y Achiever
summary: D'Metrique Godbolt, a former Power Scholar, became a Y Achiever with perfect attendance, exploring college and career opportunities. The Y Achievers program, launched in Fall 2021, helps high school students with college preparation, professional development, and career exploration.
snippet: A number of our former Power Scholars have become Y Achievers, including students like D'Metrique Godbolt, pictured at the right, as an elementary school student and now exploring college and career opportunities (and with perfect attendance as a Y Achiever)!

title: Raymond Meza's 28 Years of Service
summary: Raymond Meza has been a volunteer and advocate for the San Angelo YMCA for over twenty-eight years. He served on capital campaign committees, as Board President, and has made personal contributions for 28 consecutive years, raising over $3.1 million for the Little Explorer Preschool and Child Development Center.
program: Little Explorer Preschool and Child Development Center
snippet: Mr. Raymond Meza has been a volunteer and advocate for the San Angelo YMCA for over twenty-eight years. ... responsible for the construction of the Y's current facility and the most recent campaign committee that raised over 3.1 million dollars for the development of the Y's Little Explorer Preschool and Child Development Center.

title: Nana Otibribi III Inspires Students
summary: His Royal Highness Nana Otibribi III of Ghana visited all 10 PPEP TEC campuses at least twice during the school year, delivering uplifting and powerful messages to students.
snippet: His Royal Highness Nana Otibribi III of Ghana continued being an inspirational presence at all of our campuses

title: Fiscal Sponsorship Empowers School of Love
summary: Clay Cooke of School of Love states that Love Out Loud's Fiscal Sponsorship Program allowed them to focus 100% of their efforts on their work in 2024, calling the program indispensable to the community.
snippet: If Love Out Loud's only project was the Fiscal Sponsorship Program, it would be indispensable to our community. The FSP allowed School of Love to focus 100% of our efforts directly on our work in 2024.

title: Ashley's Journey to Nursing
summary: Ashley, a single mom of three, dreamed of becoming a Nurse Practitioner. With support from One Family Scholars, she earned her associate degree in nursing, started a job as a Registered Nurse, and is now pursuing her bachelor's degree at UMass Boston.
snippet: Ashley (above left) is an amazing mom and dedicated college student... she started her first job as a full-time Registered Nurse in the medical/surgical unit at St. Luke's Hospital in New Bedford, and aspires to work in labor & delivery or neonatal care someday soon.

title: Jackson Kunguru's Masonry Career
summary: Jackson Kunguru, a vocational training graduate, now works as a professional mason earning a skilled wage. He supports himself and his family and encourages other youth to join the program.
snippet: Jackson is a hard-working young man determined to earn a living; since graduating, he has been constantly on the move, looking for what he can do to support himself.

title: Woman 26 weeks pregnant, homeless, connected to Lifeline
summary: A woman who was 26 weeks pregnant, homeless, and had not had any prenatal care was seen on the mobile unit. The organization connected her to Lifeline, who came to see her while she was still on the mobile unit.
snippet: Last week we saw a woman who was 26 weeks pregnant, homeless, and had not had any prenatal care. We were able to connect her to Lifeline and they came to see her while she was still on the mobile unit!

title: Soup Kitchen Guest Finds Help and Lovely Atmosphere
summary: A soup kitchen guest describes CHiPS as 'lovely' and a 'big help' and 'huge help,' highlighting the welcoming environment.
snippet: 'CHiPS in one word? Lovely. It's a big help. A huge help.' -Soup Kitchen Guest

title: Board Member Testimonial on Healing
summary: A Willow Tree Board member shares that supporting the organization creates opportunities for the Holy Spirit to bring healing and wholeness to the community and beyond.
snippet: 'Supporting the work of this organization creates opportunities for the Holy Spirit to act in powerful ways that brings healing and wholeness to our community and beyond.' *Willow Tree Board Member*

title: Bernard's Lifeline at the Senior Center
summary: After his wife passed away, 85-year-old Bernard was isolated and struggling to eat enough. He was referred to Queens Community House, where Director Toolarie welcomed him to the Forest Hills Senior Center. Bernard now attends daily, exercises, enjoys hot lunches, and feels like a human being again.
snippet: I'm 85 years old and I live in Forest Hills, Queens. After my wife passed away in 2006, I was in a single, fixed income situation. ... When I called QCH, I spoke with Toolarie, the Director of the Forest Hills Senior Center. ... There's no question at all in my mind. Queens Community House staff saved my life.

title: Nicki's Experience with Racial and Social Justice Program
summary: Nicki T. found the Racial and Social Justice program enriching, noting that meeting new people and taking a hard look at oneself was challenging but supported by conversations with others in the program.
snippet: Meeting and listening to new people in various parts of the community and in different roles was the most enriching part of this experience. And, I found that taking a hard look at yourself can be challenging. Having the opportunity to talk with others in the program is a relief and source of support.

title: Camp JCC Inclusion Impact
summary: A parent shares that Camp JCC has been one of the best experiences of their son's childhood, highlighting the transformative power of the inclusive camp program for children with disabilities.
snippet: 'Camp JCC has been one of the best experiences of my son's childhood. Camp JCC changes lives.'

title: The Simpsons' Journey to Adoption
summary: Del and Sarah Simpson, unable to conceive biologically due to illness, became foster parents and adopted two siblings, Adyn and Davina. Despite obstacles from the biological father, they remained committed and found support from Adelphoi. Sarah encourages others to foster, emphasizing the rewards of providing love and a safe home.
snippet: 'We bonded with Adyn and Davina immediately and knowing the home that they would have gone to was a dangerous situation, we were definitely wanting to adopt,' she said.

title: Donors Jeanne and Nick Dowis witness program growth
summary: Jeanne and Nick Dowis of the Abram and Ray Kaplan Foundation have supported The Food Depot for over ten years. They have witnessed the growth of programs like Food 4 Kids, Diaper Depot, and mobile meal and pantry programs, and appreciate the hospitality and friendship of the organization.
snippet: The Abram and Ray Kaplan Foundation has awarded grant funds to The Food Depot for over ten years. During that time, we have been pleased to witness firsthand as programs like Food 4 Kids, Diaper Depot, and the mobile meal and pantry programs became a reality.

title: From unemployment to nursing assistant through CCMEP
summary: A 24-year-old mandated client enrolled in the CCMEP program while unemployed, pregnant, and living with her parents. After giving birth, staff helped her obtain stable housing and essential items. She then completed a Nursing Assistant Program in four weeks and was hired by a nursing center. She passed the state test, is working 40+ hours a week, and no longer receives cash assistance.
snippet: In just four weeks, she completed the Nursing Assistant Program through ASPIRE and was promptly hired by The Pavilion of Piketon Nursing Center.

title: Site Facilitator Appreciates Safe Space
summary: A site facilitator noted that SWSG provides a great space for young girls to be themselves and interact with peers outside of school, and that the diverse lessons exposed them to many new individuals.
snippet: I think SWSG is great at providing a space for young girls to be themselves and interact with their peers in a different setting outside of school. The lessons are also very diverse and exposed the girls to numerous individuals most of them had never heard of before.

title: Charles Overcomes Financial Hardship After Separation
summary: Charles had been self-sufficient for years with his wife, but after their separation he relied on a single income and fell behind on rent. The CAC assisted him with one month of overdue rent, providing stability during the transition. Following that support, Charles developed a sustainable budget, has not required further assistance, and remains steadily employed with the city.
snippet: Charles had been self-sufficient for many years, with both he and his wife working for the city. After they separated, he suddenly found himself relying on a single income and quickly fell behind on rent. We were able to assist him with one month of overdue rent, providing the stability he needed during that transition.

title: Geraldine's Safer Home Entry
summary: Geraldine received a handrail and custom built steps to safely enter and exit her home, reducing fall risk.
snippet: It is much safer for Geraldine to enter and exit her home using a handrail and custom built steps.

title: Healing Appalachia Music Fest Workshops
summary: At the Healing Appalachia Music Fest, ukuleles built and decorated by concert fans, in partnership with Mountain Grrl Experience, created a ripple effect of impact for youth. Two music workshops and four community programs were supported in Kentucky locations including a domestic violence shelter.
snippet: Two music workshops and four community programs, including a domestic violence shelter, were supported in Pikeville, Flat Gap, Shelby Valley and Martin, Kentucky.
